name: learning-basics
description: Grounding checks for the seeded knowledge base: retrieval quality, answer content and judge scores on the app's own reference docs.

cases.question: What problem does RAG solve, and what are the main stages of the pipeline?
cases.criteria: Explains that RAG grounds the model's answers in retrieved documents (reducing hallucination and staleness), and lists the pipeline stages: chunk documents, embed chunks, retrieve by similarity, generate with the retrieved context.

cases.question: How do embeddings make 'similar meaning' measurable?
cases.criteria: Explains that an embedding model maps text to a point in high-dimensional space where semantically similar texts land close together, and that similarity is measured with cosine similarity / distance.

cases.question: Why do we chunk documents, and why do consecutive chunks overlap?
cases.criteria: Explains that whole-document embeddings blur meaning so retrieval needs smaller units, and that overlap prevents answers straddling a chunk boundary from losing context.

cases.question: When should a model call a tool instead of answering directly, and how does the tool-calling loop work?
cases.criteria: Explains that tools are for things the model can't do from its weights (fresh data, exact computation, side effects), and describes the loop: model emits a structured call, the app executes it, the result goes back to the model which continues, possibly calling more tools.

cases.question: How does long-term memory work in an AI app, and what are the tradeoffs between automatic extraction and explicit memory tools?
cases.criteria: Explains that models have no built-in persistence so memory must be re-injected into prompts, contrasts automatic extraction (catches more, can be noisy) with explicit tool-based writes (precise, user-intended), and mentions similarity-based retrieval of memories.

cases.question: What is the difference between a trace and a span, and which fields matter for debugging LLM apps?
cases.criteria: Explains trace = one request's full journey, span = one timed step inside it with structured input/output, and that token usage and latency per step are what you use to find cost and quality problems.

cases.question: What kinds of checks does an eval suite combine, and why use an LLM as a judge?
cases.criteria: Explains deterministic checks (exact/substring, retrieval hits) versus rubric-based LLM judging of free-form answers, and that runs are compared over time to catch regressions from prompt or pipeline changes.
